title: Best Administrative/IT Practices When Rolling Out Custom Agents
content: Educational institutions recognizing the widespread value of artificial intelligence agents may desire to adopt the emerging technologies within their own organizations. However, the deployment of custom agents involves risks for the institutions in the form of prompt injection attacks, hallucinations, embarrassing responses, data leaks, RAG poisoning, and more. Accountability structures, proper identity and access management, and legal compliance standards (FERPA, AI Disclosure Laws, and ADA accessibility) must be maintained on an administrative level to ensure the institution can safely and efficiently deploy agentic technology. When it comes to the initial deployment of the agent, technical teams should implement guardrails, RAG databases, and rate limiting to protect against many of the associated agentic-specific risks, excluding traditional software risks. Finally, subject matter experts can review existing metrics and agent traces to adjust RAG database documents, token limits, tools, and more to ensure optimal agentic output.
